hints: State how many complete wave cycles pass a fixed point in a specified time interval.
walkthrough: Frequency counts complete oscillations or wave cycles.
For a progressive wave, it may equivalently be described as the number of wavefronts passing a fixed point per unit time.
Its SI unit is hertz, where one hertz is one cycle per second.

ai_rubric.observable: States that frequency is the number of complete wave cycles, oscillations or wavefronts passing a fixed point per unit time.

hints: Read the horizontal width of one complete cycle from the trace before using the time-base setting.
One cycle spans 4.0 cm, so calculate its period in seconds and then take the reciprocal.
walkthrough: One complete cycle on the CRO trace spans 4.0 cm horizontally.
With a time-base setting of 0.50 ms cm⁻¹, the period is T = 4.0 × 0.50 ms = 2.0 ms = 2.0 × 10⁻³ s.
Frequency is f = 1 / T = 1 / (2.0 × 10⁻³) = 500 Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the 4.0 cm horizontal cycle width and the time-base setting to obtain a period of 2.0 × 10⁻³ s.
Uses the reciprocal of the period to obtain 500 Hz.

knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The y-gain conversion from centimetres on this CRO trace to volts is supplied specifically in the question and is not a major reusable syllabus formula.

hints: Measure from the centre line to a peak, rather than using the full peak-to-peak height.
The amplitude is 2.8 cm; multiply this by the y-gain of 0.20 V cm⁻¹.
walkthrough: The vertical distance from the centre line to a peak is 2.8 cm, so this is the trace amplitude.
The y-gain is 0.20 V cm⁻¹.
Amplitude = 2.8 × 0.20 = 0.56 V.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the 2.8 cm amplitude and the 0.20 V cm⁻¹ y-gain to obtain 0.56 V.

hints: Frequency is unchanged, so retain the same horizontal spacing between matching points on successive cycles.
Use I ∝ A²: reducing intensity to one quarter reduces amplitude to one half of its original 2.8 cm value.
walkthrough: The unchanged frequency means the new trace has the same period as the original trace.
For a progressive wave, I ∝ A². Therefore I_new / I_original = 1/4 gives A_new / A_original = √(1/4) = 1/2.
The original trace amplitude is 2.8 cm, so the new amplitude is 1.4 cm from the centre line.
Sketch a smooth sinusoidal trace centred on the dashed line, with the original period and a constant 1.4 cm amplitude.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a trace with the same period as the original.
Draws a smooth sinusoidal trace with a constant amplitude smaller than 2.8 cm.
Draws the trace with amplitude 1.4 cm from the centre line.

hints: State both the circumstance in which the rule applies and how the individual displacements combine.
walkthrough: The principle applies when two or more waves overlap at the same point.
At that point and instant, add the individual displacements algebraically.
The resulting sum is the resultant displacement.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the rule applies when two or more waves meet or overlap at a point.
States that the resultant displacement is the sum of the individual displacements.

hints: An amplitude minimum is a node, and adjacent nodes are separated by half a wavelength.
The microphone begins at a node, passes three antinodes, and finishes at a node; count the node-to-node intervals before solving for λ.
walkthrough: The initial and final amplitude minima are nodes, while the three maxima lie between them at antinodes.
This path contains three adjacent node-to-node separations. Each is λ/2, so 1.05 m = 3(λ/2) = 1.5λ.
Therefore λ = 1.05 / 1.5 = 0.70 m.

ai_rubric.observable: Relates the three node-to-node intervals to 1.5 wavelengths, or states the equivalent node spacing of λ/2.

hints: Use the frequency from the CRO trace and the wavelength from the stationary-wave spacing in the wave-speed equation.
Substitute f = 500 Hz and λ = 0.70 m into v = fλ.
walkthrough: The wave equation is v = fλ.
From part (b)(i), f = 500 Hz, and from part (d)(ii), λ = 0.70 m.
Therefore v = 500 × 0.70 = 350 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the wave-speed relationship v = fλ.
Uses 500 Hz and 0.70 m to obtain 350 m s⁻¹.
